iconicAnchor.label: Botanical field sketchbook pages combining multiple observations, annotations, and watercolor studies
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Royal Botanic Gardens field and botanical sketchbook practice
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Kew's historical account contrasts polished published botanical art with personal field sketches whose watercolor studies and annotations preserve working scientific observation.

sources.title: Worth a thousand words: The hidden histories of botanical illustrations
supports: Field sketches can preserve extensive annotations around watercolor studies and function as foundational notes for later detailed work.
Unlike polished publication art, working sketches reveal a more personal process and retain evidence of observation in progress.

sources.title: Pencil and watercolour botanical sketchbook
supports: Botanical sketchbooks combine accurate observational pencil drawing with watercolor color-matching and detailed plant studies.
Working sketchbook studies can directly inform later professional botanical artwork while retaining their exploratory character.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set.
